chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Aban ibn Uthman, from a man who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed to a man and upon him was a debt. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The man should pay off whatever was upon him from his debts, and distribute what remains among the inheritors.' I said, '(Supposing) whatever he had bequeathed with from the debts gets stolen, so from which of the inheritors would it be taken for the debt?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It will not be taken from the inheritors, but the executor is responsible for it.'
ai.seo_question: Who is responsible for paying a deceased person's debt if the designated assets are lost before distribution?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the hierarchy of debt settlement, establishing that the executor (al-wasi) acts as a guarantor if the specific assets earmarked for debt repayment are lost or stolen, thereby protecting the heirs from bearing this loss. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that the executor's liability is tied to the custody of the designated assets, ensuring that the deceased's financial obligations are prioritized before any distribution to beneficiaries.
